run.question: Debug memory issues for my Python application orca in namespace app-95

report.summary: Fetched runbook python-memory-troubleshooting (skill_id python-memory-troubleshooting), which is guidance only and not evidence. Its steps and what I could do: (1) check application status — done via pods/deployments/replicasets/events; one pod app-95/orca-57fdcbf45f-v5mvp, container orca, last terminated reason OOMKilled with exitCode 137 at 2026-11-22T09:21:33Z, restartCount 1, now Running since 09:21:34Z; (2) review application logs — done, previous-instance and current-instance logs read; log lines show memory rising with processed images and reaching 114.6 MB before the kill; (3) analyse code patterns / growing collections and caches — done from logs: 'Configuration: Storing all processed images for audit trail', 'Configuration: Caching thumbnails for quick retrieval', 'Memory usage: processed_images list has N items' growing to 100, 'Cache size: N thumbnails' growing to 100 — but the application code itself lives in Secret app-95/orca-app, which cannot be read, so the source-level pattern is unverified; (4) identify memory growth patterns — done from logs (≈1.15 MB per processed image, monotonic); (5) monitor memory metrics / kubectl top — could not be carried out: Prometheus and the metrics backend returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for every query, so container working-set memory over time is unmeasured. Python-specific profiling steps (exec/debug endpoints, py-spy, tracemalloc in logs) could not be carried out because no exec/log evidence of those tools was available and the tools for exec are not part of this Run. Assessment: the orca container in app-95 is being OOM-killed because its in-process image retention and thumbnail cache grow without bound, against a 128Mi memory limit; the pod restarted in place with an unchanged pod template and was already growing again after the restart. Prometheus and Jaeger are unavailable, so no metric or trace baseline exists.

claims.text: Pod app-95/orca-57fdcbf45f-v5mvp, container orca, has restartCount 1 with lastState.terminated reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, startedAt 2026-11-22T09:21:01Z, finishedAt 2026-11-22T09:21:33Z, and is currently running (started 2026-11-22T09:21:34Z) with Ready=True and QoS class Burstable.

The previous orca container's logs show the process-reported stored-image memory growing monotonically with processed images: 'Approximate memory used by stored images: 10.3 MB' at 10 images (09:21:02Z), 33.8 MB at 30, 55.9 MB at 50, 77.0 MB at 70, 102.9 MB at 90 and '114.6 MB' with 'processed_images list has 100 items' and 'Cache size: 100 thumbnails' at 09:21:31Z, followed by log output ending at 09:21:33.6Z.

The same orca logs state the retention configuration in effect at startup: 'Configuration: Storing all processed images for audit trail' and 'Configuration: Caching thumbnails for quick retrieval', and the size-tracking lines 'Memory usage: processed_images list has N items' and 'Cache size: N thumbnails' increase by 10 every 10 images with no reduction or eviction line observed.

Deployment app-95/orca runs 1 replica of container orca with image python:3.9-slim and resources limits memory 128Mi / requests cpu 10m, memory 64Mi; its only environment variables are PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 and SERVICE_NAME=orca-image-processor, and the application directory /app is mounted from secret orca-app.

The restart happened in place inside the same pod and same ReplicaSet, not by a rollout: the pod name stayed orca-57fdcbf45f-v5mvp, only its container restarted (Pod 'Created' and 'Started' events count 2, first 09:21:00Z, last 09:21:34Z), and ReplicaSet orca-57fdcbf45f has owner Deployment orca with one 'SuccessfulCreate' event at 09:21:00Z and no delete event.

After the restart the new container instance shows the same growth pattern and is already at 'Approximate memory used by stored images: 22.9 MB' with 20 processed images at 09:21:37Z, so the condition that produced the OOM kill is recurring in the running instance.

The only ConfigMap present in namespace app-95 is kube-root-ca.crt (the cluster CA bundle); no ConfigMap in app-95 holds application settings, and the Deployment's env carries no memory, cache or retention settings.

The node hosting the pod, opspilot-m1-control-plane, reports MemoryPressure=False, DiskPressure=False, PIDPressure=False and Ready=True at query time, so the OOM kill is a container-limit event rather than node-level memory pressure.

Most likely cause: the orca application retains every processed image in an in-process list and caches every thumbnail with no eviction, growing ≈1.15 MB per image, which exhausts the container's 128Mi memory limit after roughly 100 images and produces the OOMKilled exit 137 at 2026-11-22T09:21:33Z; the Deployment app-95/orca (container orca, application files from Secret orca-app) is the object that carries this behavior and limit.

Contributing factor: the 128Mi memory limit with a 64Mi request is below what this workload's image batch accumulates within about 33 seconds of processing, so the limit makes the OOM kill arrive early; raising the limit alone would defer but not remove the failure while retention stays unbounded.

Node-level memory exhaustion on opspilot-m1-control-plane as the cause of the kill is rejected: the node reports MemoryPressure=False and Ready=True while the pod's own container last termination reason is OOMKilled at its 128Mi cgroup limit.

Cap the retention: bound processed_images (for example collections.deque(maxlen=...) or process-and-discard with streaming) and use an LRU/TTL-bounded thumbnail cache (functools.lru_cache with maxsize or a TTL cache), so memory stops scaling with the number of images.

After the retention is bounded, right-size the container: raise the memory limit above the measured working set for the intended batch size and align the request with it, and add a container memory working-set alert (container_memory_working_set_bytes against the limit) so growth is visible before the next OOM kill.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable for this Run (get_metric_names, metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query and get_prometheus_target all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so container_memory_working_set_bytes / container_memory_usage_bytes and any historical memory trend for app-95/orca remain unmeasured; this is unknown, not zero.
Jaeger was unreachable (traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), and 'orca' is not among the listed trace service names, so no trace error-rate or latency signal for orca was checked.

The application code is stored in Secret app-95/orca-app, which cannot be read, so the exact retention code, the flags behind 'Storing all processed images for audit trail' and 'Caching thumbnails for quick retrieval', and whether any injected growth setting exists in the code could not be verified.

Events returned for the window contain no kubelet OOMKilling or Evicted event for this pod; the OOM kill is attested only by the container's lastState termination reason and the log cutoff at 09:21:33.6Z, and event history before the pod's 09:21:00Z creation is unknown.
The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so who or what created the Deployment/pod at 2026-11-22T09:21:00Z and whether orca ran and was OOM-killed earlier cannot be determined.

Root cause naming is bounded by the unreadable code: the Deployment app-95/orca is named because its container carries the limit and mounts the application files, but the specific source lines implementing the unbounded retention were not observed.
next_steps: Read the application code in Secret orca-app (or its source repository) and locate the processed_images list and thumbnail cache to bound them (deque maxlen, LRU/TTL cache) or stream processing with discard.

Restore Prometheus/Jaeger connectivity and graph container_memory_working_set_bytes{namespace="app-95",pod=~"orca.*"} against the 128Mi limit to confirm the sawtooth growth and the time-to-OOM per restart.
Consider a temporary memory limit increase only as a stopgap while bounding retention, since the observed growth is monotonic per processed image.
Check change history for app-95/orca (integration not available here) to confirm when the retention configuration and the 128Mi limit were introduced.
